absolute coordinate bound beta_1*beta_2
first-order SwiGLU agreement near zero
pointwise SwiGLU limit as both betas increase
finite input gradients on negative, origin, moderate, and saturated regions
one shared down-projection before every routed expert
selected raw-weighted routed aggregate
one RMSNorm after aggregation and before the shared up-projection
full-width shared-expert sum
manual forward parity and finite input/projection/expert/norm gradients
route uniqueness, conservation, non-negativity, and shape rejection
normalized_LatentMoE.expert_network_scope: callable shape-preserving functions; expert internals are deliberately outside Eq. 11 qualification

checks: bias affects top-k selection but not selected mixture weights
stable lower-index tie breaking is explicit local reference policy
top-(k+1) biased cutoff
required bias r_ij equals cutoff_i minus raw score_ij

mean-centered returned bias
common old-bias offset invariance
integral target load required by the exact finite-batch oracle
exact_Quantile_Balancing.causality: the function returns a next-step bias and never reroutes its input batch with that bias

checks: adaptive [b_min-1,b_max+1] range and width
int64 per-expert counts
exact count additivity across arbitrary microbatch and rank partitions
first cumulative bin reaching ceil(m*k/n)
source within-bin interpolation formula
mean-centered returned bias
estimate lies within one bin width of the valid empirical quantile interval

histogram_Quantile_Balancing.finite_sample_convention: exact Eq. 14 chooses the upper endpoint of the load-q empirical threshold interval; histogram interpolation may choose another valid point in or within one bin of that interval, so representative equality is not required
